While Rebar is fun to work with and is good for hammering practive, any grade of it tends to be "mystery-metal". The grade is not about carbon content, but rather tensile strength, so little to no control over impurities is implied. It's your dad's Buick, grandma's refrigerator, etc... whatever made it into the melting pot. The grading system means it will endure tension to a certain specification, but all the other junk in there means that even from one section of bar to another, the chemistry may be different.

What this means, is that while you may be able to forge the shape of a knife from it, and even occasionally get lucky on heat treatment of the most basic kind, you'll never be able to control the heat treatment with mastery, always guessing from piece to piece. Since HT is the soul of a knife, and the mark of a knifemaker, it pays not to waste too much time on the novelty of scrap steel when good known material is so cheaply and easily had.
